title: How a Purified Water project runs, from order to water in use | Aquemi
meta: Stages, hold points and durations for your Purified Water package: who signs each stage, who does what, and changes after approval.
headline: How a project runs, from order to water in use
lead: Plan your approvals and qualification time from one schedule, with who signs each stage. Your contact from order to handover: a project lead named in your order.
primary_cta_intent: Not sure yet: talk to an engineer

blocks.h: Stages, what each leaves, and who signs
blocks.intro: Total: set in your project schedule, counted from the start event stated in your proposal, plus your review time. Replacing a system? We plan the cutover; production stops only for a shutdown agreed with you.

items.d: Your user requirement specification (URS), capital approval and supplier approval. They come before our clock starts, so plan them first.
Basis of design, piping and instrumentation diagrams and functional specification. Under good manufacturing practice (GMP), design qualification (DQ) closes this stage.
items.hold: You, and your quality unit for DQ under GMP

items.d: You review drawings for fabrication in a period agreed with you. Lead time to delivery is stated in your proposal.
Skids built in our Ontario shop and tested with water before they ship.
With water, to the protocol you or your quality unit approved. Leaves raw data, deviation log, report and release to ship.
Drained after FAT, then shipped. Kept until start-up under conditions set out in your proposal.
Installation to the scope set out in your proposal. Tie-in during the planned shutdown. Leaves the SAT report.
items.hold: You, or your quality unit under GMP

items.d: To protocols your quality unit approves; leaves reports and draft procedures. Without GMP: commissioning and an acceptance test against your specification.
items.hold: Your quality unit, or you without GMP

items.t: PQ under GMP: three phases, at least 12 months
items.d: Performance qualification (PQ). After at least 2 weeks of sampling, your quality unit releases the water for use.

blocks.h: Who does what, and what is ready before installation
blocks.intro: Your proposal marks every task and hand-off: by us, supplied only, or by you. Installation follows the scope set out in your proposal.
rows: You: project manager, site head or safety lead
Own the schedule, the order and site access. Name one contact who approves drawings and changes.

rows.t: Work permits: chemicals, drain and isolation points for your safety team

rows: Approves the URS, each protocol before it runs and each report after. Decides first use from PQ data.
Validation master plan; SAT, IQ and OQ protocols approved
Your engineer writes or reviews the URS and may witness FAT. Your mechanical, electrical and plumbing trades review our drawings.
Drawing comments closed in writing before fabrication [confirm]
Builds the room and brings utilities to the battery limits.

rows.t: Power, feed water and drain at the battery limits, set per project

rows: Designs, builds and tests the package. Drafts each protocol, executes it through engineers named in your proposal and writes the report.
Your site readiness checklist, sent before delivery [confirm]

items.q: How long do our own approvals add?
items.a: Count them in your plan. Capital approval, supplier qualification and URS sign-off come before our clock starts. Your review time at each hold adds to the durations above, unless a stage says it is included.

items.q: Do these stages apply if we are not under GMP?
items.a: Yes. Commissioning and an acceptance test against your specification take the place of qualification. The DQ signature and PQ apply under GMP only; you sign the other holds and release the water.

items.q: What if our site is not ready on time?
items.a: Tell us as soon as you know. We agree a new delivery date and where the skids wait, under conditions set out in your proposal. Storage and extra visits cost what your proposal sets out. The readiness checklist reaches you ahead of delivery, on a date agreed with you [confirm].

items.q: What if we change something after approving the drawings?
items.a: You get one page first: the reason, the price and the effect on the schedule. Work on that item waits for your written approval [confirm].

items.q: Can the skids wait through a Canadian winter before start-up?
items.a: Only under conditions set out in your proposal. Frozen or dried-out reverse osmosis membranes may need replacing before start-up. Plan indoor storage if delivery comes before your room is ready.

items.q: What do we pay at each stage?
items.a: Payment follows events, not dates, through milestones set out in your proposal. The terms are on Buying from Aquemi.

cta.h: Tell us your target date for water in use
cta.body: An engineer works back from it to your order date and holds. Cost: quoted in your proposal.
